quote: I used to stay out until midnight. Now I'm in bed by nine, awake by two, and thinking about something I said in 1998.
I don't say "no" to plans anymore. I say "let me check" and never check.
I used to worry about being late. Now I worry about being early and having to make conversation.
Every year I learn to say no. Every year I volunteer for something by February.
I don't forget names. I file them somewhere I can't reach.
My plans for the day: nothing. I'm protecting it.
I used to chase dreams. Now I chase the one hour a day when the house is quiet.
I clean for company, then spend the whole visit apologizing for a mess I can't see.
I bought a planner to get organized. The planner is gorgeous. I've now lost the planner.
My phone has six hundred contacts and I answer four of them.
